title: Fluorescence imaging detection of nanodomain redox signaling events at organellar contacts
protocol: Immerse 100 25 mm No1.5 coverslips in 70% ethanol one-by-one.
Let the coverslips soak, covered, for a minimum of 1 hour.
Allow coverslips to fully dry in a sterile laminar-flow cabinet by propping them against the edge of individual open 35 mm cell culture dishes.
Dissolve 3.1 g boric acid and 4.35 g sodium borate into 800 mL of 18.2 MΩ water, check/adjust to pH 8.5, then make up to 1 L with water.
Filter the solution to 0.2 μm and store at 4°C for up to 6 months.
Dilute 5 mL of 10× poly-D-lysine solution to 1× using 45 mL of sterile 0.1M Borate buffer, mix well.
Add 500 μL of the 1× poly-D-lysine solution to each coverslip surface in a horizontal position within culture dishes.
Incubate the coverslips with the poly-D-lysine solution for 15 minutes at room temperature.
Wash coverslips twice with 2 mL of 18.2 MΩ water per coverslip.
Expose coverslips to sterilizing UV for 1 hour.
Store covered culture dishes containing coverslips in a sterile environment at 4°C–25°C for up to 14 days.
Seed 30,000-40,000 cells in 300 μL of cell culture medium per coverslip on day 2.
Place seeded coverslips in an incubator for attachment.
Confirm cell attachment by microscopy at approximately 4 hours.
Add standard cell culture media to a total volume of 2 mL/35 mm dish.
Remove Lipofectamine TM 3000 kit reagents from the refrigerator and place on wet ice.
Ensure plasmid DNA is purified to a concentration >1 μg/μL in TE buffer.
Prepare 1 μg of plasmid DNA per coverslip in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, with a bias toward ER-surface targeted linker if applicable.
Add 100 μL of Opti-MEM per coverslip to the Eppendorf tube and mix gently.
Add 1 μL of P3000 reagent per coverslip and mix again.
Prepare another tube by adding 100 μL of Opti-MEM and 1 μL of Lipofectamine 3000 per coverslip, mixing well.
Combine the contents of both tubes, mix by inverting, and incubate for 15-30 minutes.
Add 200 μL of transfection solution dropwise to each 2 mL media containing cells on coverslips.
Incubate with transfection solution for a minimum of 24 hours, preferably 36 hours before imaging.
Prepare a 200 mM H2O2 solution in 1 mL water and store on ice up to 8 hours.
Prepare a 1 M dithiothreitol (DTT) solution in 1 mL water and store on ice, replacing every 3 hours.
Pre-warm pre-imaging/imaging solutions in a 37°C water bath.
Create a 25 μM solution of TMRM in DMSO via serial dilution in a laminar flow cabinet.
Remove cell culture media from coverslip.
Wash coverslip with 2% BSA pre-imaging buffer.
Incubate coverslip in 2 mL pre-imaging buffer containing 25 nM of TMRM for 30 minutes at 37°C shaking water bath set at 25 spm.
Ensure all subsequent washing/imaging solutions contain a TMRM concentration of 25 nM.
Clean the Attofluor cell chamber and gasket with surgical instrument cleaner.
Wash the chamber with 70% ethanol.
Rinse the chamber with distilled water.
Clean the coverslip with imaging buffer.
Transfer the coverslip to the cell chamber using fine forceps.
Add 1 mL of imaging buffer containing 25 nM TMRM to the chamber.
Carefully clean the lower surface of the coverslip with Kimtech wipes.
Check for leaks in the imaging chamber.
Place the imaging chamber in a heated stage insert.
Apply a drop of low fluorescence immersion oil to the objective.
Focus the microscope on the cell field using brightfield transmitted light.
Locate cells with bright ER-dominant Grx1roGFP2 fluorescence under 480 nm excitation.

Adjust Grx1roGFP2 fluorescence intensity and duration so that 402 nm emission is approximately 1/2, 480 nm is approximately 3/4, and TMRE is approximately 1/6 to 1/4 of the camera's dynamic range (10-15,000 out of 65,535).
Record a baseline using 2–6 s interval time-lapse imaging.
Remove approximately 30% of the imaging solution from the chamber.
Add 100 nM rapamycin to the chamber and mix well.
Return the mixture to the imaging chamber.
Incubate cells with rapamycin for 3 minutes in HepG2 cells.
Stop linker reaction by removing rapamycin.
Incubate with 2 μM FK506 for 5 minutes.
Replace the imaging solution after incubation.
Allow approximately 5 minutes for recovery and temperature stabilization of the imaging chamber/solution.
Set the time-lapse imaging protocol to record image sets at intervals less than 10 seconds.
Calibrate Grx1roGFP2 as necessary.
Remove approximately 300 μL media from the cell culture.
Add 1 mM DTT from a 1 M stock solution to the cell culture.
Gently mix and monitor Grx1roGFP2 emission wavelengths.
When the signal stabilizes, add another pulse of 1 mM DTT.
If no further response is observed, this confirms complete reduction of the probe.
Wash out the DTT using 3–4 chamber volumes of imaging media containing 200 μM H2O2 from a 200 mM stock solution and pre-warmed to appropriate temperature.
Once Grx1roGFP2 emission stabilizes again, add another pulse of 200 μM H2O2.
If the probe is completely oxidized, no further ratio change will be observed.
Depolarize mitochondria by adding 10 μM FCCP and 2.5 μg/μL oligomycin.
Maintain 25 nM TMRM in all solutions.
Collect images to monitor TMRM fluorescence, showing a rapid decrease in mitochondrial signal followed by an elevation due to movement of TMRM into the cytosol.
Continue image collection until TMRM equilibrates across the plasma membrane to establish a lower limit.
Replace DTT aliquots frequently to ensure freshness and avoid degradation with oxygen exposure.
Apply fresh 200 μM H2O2 solution multiple times after DTT application to remove residual DTT and allow full oxidation of Grx1roGFP2.
Ensure that wavelengths move in opposite directions in response to both DTT and H2O2 applications for accurate analysis.
Process microscope time-lapse image files using Fiji (ImageJ) to remove background noise and movement.
Identify flicker events and subsequent oxidative bursts from the processed images.
Assign regions of interest (ROIs) to extract spatiotemporal information from the events.
Convert microscope files from each wavelength to .tif format using Fiji (ImageJ).
Open the converted .tif files as 3 independent image stacks derived from the 402 nm, 480 nm & 577 nm excitation wavelengths.
Calibrate ImageJ images with the microscope settings: Analyze>Set Scale, setting pixel size to 0.4 μm.
Crop the image stacks to a single cell area (∼150 × 150 pixels or 60 × 60 μm).
Select an area that is clear background in the entire time course of all three wavelength image stacks.
Run Process>Subtract background for each image stack using the selected background area.
Install MultiStackReg 1.45 by dragging and dropping “Multistackreg1.45.jar” into Fiji’s “plugins” folder and restarting the program.
Select the brightest, most stable stack (usually the 480 nm emission of reduced Grx1roGFP2).
Run Plugins>Registration>MultiStackReg with default “Rigid Body” settings selected.
Save the transformation file under a suitable name.
Apply registration using the saved transformation file.
Apply the saved transformation parameters to the two remaining stacks by running MultiStackReg again and selecting “Load Transformation File”.
Run median filter on each image stack by selecting Process>Filters>Median3D, with X:2 Y:2 Z:2 settings.
Create a copy of the 577 nm (TMRM) stack.
Convert the copied TMRM stack to 8-bit and save it.
Run Analyze>Multi Kymograph>Stack Difference on each image stack, selecting 1 frame difference.
Rename and save the resultant stack after running Multi Kymograph.
Denoise the image stack by running Process>Noise>Remove Outliers with Radius: 2 Threshold 5 settings.
Adjust brightness and contrast to identify flickers clearly.
Move through the image stack frame-by-frame to draw ROIs for flicker events.
Draw ROIs manually using the polygon selection tool or magic wand tool.
Save each ROI to the ROI manager.
Save the complete set of ROIs at the end.
Use the ROI set to make measurements of flickers.
Set Measurements can be used in the Results window to measure ROI area indicating mitochondrial area subject to depolarization.
Use Set Measurements>Results>Mean gray value to extract time-course raw data following selection of desired ROIs.
Use More>Multi Measure in the ROI manager for multiple measurements.
Establish a local baseline (F0) preceding the flicker as the stable fluorescence of the target mitochondrion.
Establish the local minimum fluorescence (Fmin), i.e., the lowest fluorescence value following depolarization.
Subtract Fmin from raw fluorescence values (F) and divide by baseline value (F0).
Normalize flickers’ fluorescence using the established method.
Set up Region of Interest (ROI) for measuring oxidative bursts.
Apply each ROI to the two processed image stacks derived from 402 nm and 480 nm excitation wavelengths of Grx1roGFP2.
Use ROI manager > more > multi measure with Results > Set Measurements > Mean Gray Value checked.
Copy and paste values into a spreadsheet.
Create ratio of F402/F480 for each measurement point.
Calibrate the Grx1roGFP ratio output using values from fully reduced & oxidized conditions.
Carefully check regions of interest (ROIs) to ensure consistent representation of the underlying region of cell.
Monitor mitochondrial dynamics for potential movement into/out of an ROI or fusion/fission events that might compromise fluorescence data and subsequent analysis.
Enlarge the ROI to cover the whole area before and after slight movements to offset minor displacement.
